picked.t: 베트남 진출 유럽기업 10곳 중 6곳 ‘경영성과 좋음’…3분기 BCI 78.3
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남에서 사업 중인 유럽 기업들이 베트남 경제에 대해 낙관적인 전망을 유지했다. 주베트남 유럽상공회의소(EuroCham·유로참)가 15일 내놓은 ‘2026년 3분기 기업신뢰지수(Business Confidence Index, BCI)’ 보고서에 따르면, 3분기 BCI는 78.3을 나타냈다. 2분기와 비교하면 1.4포인트 내린 것이나, 여전히 역사적으로 높은 수준을 유지했다. 이에 대해 유로참은 “경영 환경의 지속적인 어려움 속에서도 투자자들의 신뢰가 여전히 견고함을 보여주는 것”이라고 평가했다. 유로참의 설문에 참여한 기업 중 약 64%는 현재 경영 성과를 ‘좋음’ 또는 ‘매우 좋음”으로 평가했다. 28%는 중립적이거나 신중한 입장이었는데, 국제 수요가 둔화한 데다 더 명확한 정책, 빠른 행정 절차, 예측 가능한 결과를 기다리는 기업들의 심리가 반영된 데 따른 것이라는 평가다. 브루노 야스파에르트(Bruno Jaspaert) 유로참 회장은 “베트남 경제가 강한 성장 모멘텀을 유지하고 있다”고 말했다. 실제로 베트남의 3분기 국내총생산(GDP)은 전년 동기 대비 9.95%, 1~9월 누계로는 9.01% 성장했다. 그는 "전 세계 불확실성이 큰 가운데 베트남은 두 자릿수 성장이라는 목표에 가까워지고 있다. 이제 중요한 과제는 예측 가능성을 높이고 회복력을 강화하고 개혁을 공고히 해, 기업이 더 많은 에너지를 가치 창출에 쏟게 하면서 성장을 경제 전반에서 체감하게 만드는 것"이라고 강조했다. 부문별 실적은 엇갈렸다. 농업·식품 밸류체인은 신뢰 점수가 11.7포인트 올라 83.9로 가장 크게 개선됐다. 투입 비용 부담과 역내 수입품과의 경쟁에도 오른 것이다. 무역·물류·소비재도 높은 실적을 이어갔는데, 이는 역내 생산과 국경 간 교역에서 베트남이 담당하는 역할을 보여준다는 평가다. 반면 관광·호텔업은 직전 분기에 좋은 실적을 낸 뒤 22.5포인트 떨어져 67.9가 됐다. 소비자 지출 변화와 운영비, 이상 기후에 취약한 업종이라는 점이 드러났다는 분석이다. 시장 성향별 신뢰 점수는 베트남 내수 시장 중심 기업이 80.4로 가장 높았고, 유럽연합(EU) 중심 73.2, 미국 중심 70.7, 아세안 중심 73.9 순을 나타냈다. 3분기 BCI는 전반적으로 긍정적인 모습을 보였으나, 행정·규제 장벽으로 인해 기업들이 갖는 부담은 여전했다. 자세히 살펴보면, 응답자의 93%는 규제·행정 문제와 세무·재무 절차가 사업에 영향을 준다고 답했고, 기업들은 평균 8개의 성장 저해 요인에 직면하고 있다고 했다. 가장 자주 꼽힌 장애물은 행정 절차와 서류 작업으로 응답자의 60%였다. 불명확하거나 일관성 없는 규정이 53%, 세무 행정 문제가 52%, 인재 부족이 49%로 뒤를 이었다. 야스파에르트 회장은 “투명한 법률 체계와 일관된 안내가 사업 환경 개선에 필수”라며 "차이를 만드는 것은 무엇이 필요한지 알고, 일관된 안내를 받고, 절차가 대략 얼마나 걸릴지 합리적으로 예측할 수 있는지가 핵심"이라고 말했다. 조사에서 긍정적인 점도 있었다. 응답자 10명 중 9명은 베트남을 투자처로 추천하겠다고 답했다. 63%는 베트남에서 5년 이상 사업할 계획이고, 23%는 20년을 넘는 장기 전망을 갖고 있었다. 기업들은 베트남의 주요 강점으로 숙련 노동력, 경쟁력 있는 비용, 정치·거시경제 안정을 꼽았다. 내수 시장, 폭넓은 자유무역협정(FTA) 네트워크, 글로벌 공급망이 재편되는 가운데 베트남이 확보한 전략적 위치도 언급됐다. 유로참은 행정 결정을 빠르게 하고, 규제를 국제 표준에 맞추고, 디지털 공공 서비스를 확대하면 베트남의 장기적인 투자 매력이 커질 수 있다고 조언했다. 베트남 정부에 바라는 점에 대해 응답자의 37%는 더 빠른 행정 결정을 최우선 과제로 꼽았고, 35%는 국제 표준에 맞춘 규제 정비를, 더 빠르고 전면 디지털화된 정부 서비스를 요구한 기업도 35%에 달했다.

picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City metro line stops running for 1 hour after power outage
picked.body: The incident began at around 7:04 a.m., when the entire 220 kV Thu Duc substation lost power due to a fault in the national power transmission system. Trains operating at the time were directed to the nearest stations, where passengers were asked to disembark and wait for services to resume. According to HURC1, the line’s operator, the power outage affected 14 trains. Services resumed at 7:57 a.m., after the power system was fixed and the company worked with the Southern Power System Dispatch Center to restore the supply. A HURC1 representative said the electricity system supporting metro operations depends on the national power grid. The incident marked the first time the Ben Thanh–Suoi Tien line had experienced a service disruption caused by a power failure originating from the grid. Since beginning commercial operations in December 2024, the line has experienced several disruptions caused by lightning strikes, which triggered electrical protection systems, forcing trains to stop as a safety precaution. The most recent incident occurred on Oct. 7, when a lightning strike near Tan Cang Station disrupted services for approximately four minutes. Disruptions due to power outages have happened to metro systems worldwide. In August 2025, Japan’s Osaka metro suspended services across the entire Chuo Line following a power supply problem. Some sections resumed operations overnight, but full service was not restored until the following morning, affecting the travel plans of tens of thousands of passengers. The Ben Thanh–Suoi Tien, HCMC's only running metro line, stretches nearly 20 km, comprising three underground stations and 11 elevated stations. It connects the city center with its eastern part. The line uses 17 trains, each consisting of three carriages. In its first year of operation, the metro line served approximately 19 million passenger trips, averaging 52,000 trips per day. By March 2026, daily ridership had risen to around 70,000 passenger trips.

picked.t: Vietnam targets at least 10% GDP growth in 2027
picked.body: As the government expects 2027 to be a year of acceleration and breakthroughs, it also targets GDP per capita of $6,100, consumer price index growth at around 4.5%, and average labor productivity growth at 8.6%, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung told lawmakers at a meeting Saturday morning. The government also seeks breakthroughs in mobilizing, allocating and efficiently using all resources for development. It aims to increase budget revenue by 9.1% and curb recurrent spending. To diversify funding sources, the government plans to issue various types of bonds, secure official development assistance loans, mobilize credit and private resources, increase investment by state-owned enterprises and encourage foreign-invested companies to reinvest their profits in Vietnam. Hung pledged to continue managing interest rates and exchange rates appropriately. He said decisive and effective measures would be introduced to lower lending rates and direct credit toward production and business activities, exports, science and technology, and small and medium-sized enterprises. The government will also accelerate economic restructuring, renew the development model and strengthen the economy’s internal capacity, independence, self-reliance and resilience. It plans to expand the domestic industrial ecosystem, prioritizing foundational and supporting industries. Modern service and logistics hubs and special economic zones will be established. Reporting on the results for 2026, Hung said 14 of the 15 socioeconomic indicators were expected to meet or exceed their targets. GDP grew 9.95% in the third quarter and 9.01% in the first nine months, placing Vietnam among the fastest-growing economies in Southeast Asia and in the world. He said fiscal, monetary and other macroeconomic policies had been managed proactively and flexibly. Full-year budget revenue is estimated at VND3.06 quadrillion (US$118.2 billion), up 14%. Hung said the State Bank of Vietnam had directed credit institutions to jointly reduce lending rates by 1.5–2 percentage points for production and business activities and priority sectors, in line with directives from the Party’s central leadership and the government. Credit ratings agency Moody’s revised Vietnam’s sovereign credit outlook from "stable" to "positive" in May, while the stock market’s status was upgraded to Secondary Emerging Market in September. "International organizations have praised Vietnam’s resilience and growth prospects," the PM said. The government’s report also showed that industry and construction grew 11.21% in the first nine months, the highest rate since 2015. Foreign trade rose 30.4% and is estimated to reach $1.11 trillion for the full year, potentially surpassing the $1 trillion mark for the first time. Total investment across the economy reached VND3.11 quadrillion in the first nine months, up 15.1%. Public investment disbursement totaled nearly VND643 trillion, equivalent to 63% of the plan and almost 13% higher than a year earlier. Registered foreign direct investment reached $50.36 billion, up 76.4% and the highest level since 2021. On infrastructure, Vietnam completed another 395 kilometers of expressways and opened the entire eastern North-South Expressway to traffic. The government also took decisive steps to resolve problems affecting stalled and long-delayed projects. By the end of September, problems at 4,688 projects had either been resolved or had resolution plans in place. These projects cover nearly 196,000 hectares and have total investment exceeding VND3.2 quadrillion. The political and legal framework for fully resolving obstacles affecting wind power, solar power and mineral projects, among others, was also completed. For the remainder of the year, Hung said the government would "strive to achieve the best possible results, especially double-digit growth alongside macroeconomic stability and inflation control." The government will take decisive and effective measures to lower lending rates and ensure electricity and fuel supplies. "Localities must strive for the highest possible growth, especially the major growth hubs," he said. Presenting the appraisal report, Phan Van Mai, chairman of the National Assembly’s Economic and Financial Committee, said the committee commended the decisive and flexible leadership of the government and prime minister, as well as the efforts of ministries, agencies and localities. However, the committee highlighted six issues requiring the government’s attention in its management in the coming period. It said growth remained strong but rested on an uncertain foundation. Specifically, the four largest local economies – HCMC, Hanoi, Hai Phong and Dong Nai – which account for nearly 47% of gross regional domestic product, were all expected to miss their 2026 growth targets. picked.t: IPP Travel Retail opens Travel Essentials store at Cam Ranh airport
picked.body: IPP Travel Retail opened its Travel Essentials store at Cam Ranh International Airport's international terminal on Sept. 30, combining practical travel products with locally inspired gifts and souvenirs. Cam Ranh serves Nha Trang and Khanh Hoa Province, connecting Vietnam's south-central coast with international markets. In 2025, the airport handled nearly 7.3 million passengers, including about 4.7 million international travelers. More than 30 airlines operate at the airport, which added 13 airlines and 14 routes in 2025, including connections to Seoul, Busan and Chengdu. The opening ceremony was attended by representatives of Cam Ranh International Terminal, airport authorities, partner brands and IPP Travel Retail. Phillip Nguyen, Vice President of IPPG and CEO of IPP Travel Retail, said the store aims to meet travelers' immediate needs while introducing Vietnamese culture to international visitors. "Every passenger who passes through here is an opportunity for us to introduce Vietnam to friends from around the world," he said. Travel Essentials features three main product categories: Travel Tech, offering electronic devices and accessories; Kids Toys & Hobbies, catering to children and families; and Local Gifts, featuring souvenirs and regional specialties. "We wanted more than just a convenience store. We wanted to understand what travelers need for their trip and help them take a little piece of Vietnam with them when they leave, through local gifts and our little friend TIPPI," Nguyen said. The store also introduced TIPPI, a mascot designed to represent the brand and its connection to Vietnamese culture. TIPPI features a rounded, cloud-like shape and friendly expression, wearing a traditional Vietnamese conical hat ( non la ) decorated with the national flag and an ao ba ba , a garment associated with southern Vietnam.
